trust_decision.summary: The admin console's /download/* servlet decides which admin REST operation to run from request query parameters, is authenticated only by the FORM-auth session cookie, and each ContentSource re-attaches the REST token read from that session server-side, so a cross-site GET can drive admin REST commands without any per-request anti-forgery token.

landing_point.why: A reader told only 'admin console CSRF' follows the one servlet that turns an incoming GET/POST into a privileged admin REST call; doGet forwards straight to doPost and no origin/anti-forgery check is made anywhere on that path.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The RestUtil *FromServlet helpers are a generic client API written for JSF handlers, so enforcing an anti-forgery token there reads as the caller's job; the /download/* paths likewise look like read-only file downloads rather than admin actions.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate console downloads are opened as cross-page GETs (iframe.src / window.location) with query parameters and must keep working; a fix that requires POST or a request header breaks client-stub, log-file archive and log-viewer downloads.

O6_input_shapes: HTTP method: GET is forwarded to doPost, so the state-changing path accepts both (DownloadServlet.java:154-156)
contentSourceId selects which admin REST operation runs (DownloadServlet.java:212-231; WEB-INF/web.xml:119-126)
restUrl query parameter chooses the outbound admin REST base address (LogFilesContentSource.java:89-94; LogViewerContentSource.java:84-91; ClientStubsContentSource.java:87-92)
scalar query parameters target, start, instanceName, appName (LogFilesContentSource.java:88,102-104; LogViewerContentSource.java:85-86; ClientStubsContentSource.java:86)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: DownloadServlet dispatches on the request's contentSourceId and accepts GET for every registered ContentSource, so the servlet-level route reaches the same REST sink independently of any per-content-source check.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the read-only download entry point and the three known content sources are the only real targets, so it looks like infrastructure rather than a protected action.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the three content sources (1 file)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Any ContentSource class named in the ContentSources servlet init-param is invoked with no check; the set of sources is configuration data, not code the fix touches.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Adding a new source is a deployment/config change outside the fixed Java classes.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: war module, one module away from the servlet code

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The public RestUtil post/put/delete/get helpers reach the same admin REST sink with the session's REST token and no anti-forgery token, and are callable from any JSF handler.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: They are server-side helpers that only run after JSF authentication, so they look exempt from request-origin checks.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: admingui/common util package, one package from the servlet package

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A fourth DownloadServlet.ContentSource, e.g. a thread-dump or server-log archive download, built by copying LogFilesContentSource.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The ContentSources init-param is the servlet's designed extension point and the three existing classes are copy-paste templates with the same request-parameter-to-REST-call shape.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another JSF page that builds a /download/... URL and opens it with iframe.src or window.location.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The console has many resource pages that generate download links in exactly this way, so a new feature would repeat the pattern without a token.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another REST-verb helper that attaches the session REST token to an outbound call with no anti-forgery parameter.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class already duplicates the same token-attach snippet across seven methods, so a maintainer adding a verb would copy it.

O9_family: cross-site request forgery: state-changing admin routes authenticated only by an ambient session cookie, with no per-request anti-forgery token

O10_build.toolchain: Maven aggregator, javase.version 21 (pom.xml:234-235); affected modules appserver/admingui/common and appserver/admingui/war
O10_build.project_tests: Selenium admin-console devtests exist (appserver/admingui/devtests LogViewerTest.java, SecurityTest.java) and need a running domain plus a browser; no unit test covers the /download/* CSRF path at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Block GET (or require a header) in DownloadServlet.doPost only, which breaks the console's iframe/window.location downloads and leaves the per-source entry points and RestUtil helpers open.

out_of_scope_notes: Adjacent but outside this advisory: the restUrl query parameter is concatenated into the outbound admin REST endpoint (LogFilesContentSource.java:89-94, LogViewerContentSource.java:84-91), which looks like a separate SSRF/token-leak issue; not pursued.
